optionReasons.saa-avc-011:option:0: On-demand of a single type is the most expensive option — does not minimize cost or diversify capacity.
optionReasons.saa-avc-011:option:2: It's the closest because Reserved Instances of 3 years give great discount for real — but stop fixed capacity of ONE type by 3 years, without the resilience the interruption that the load tolerates nor the flexibility of thousands of different instances; for pausable batch, Spot diversified with failback On-Demand delivers more economy.
optionReasons.saa-avc-011:option:3: Migratory to Lambda 'without adjustments' ignores the limit of 15 min and the execution model — does not fit in batch of thousands of instances.

finalJustifications: Because Auto Scaling with Spot of multiple types (capacity-optimized) and failure On-Demand cuts the cost to the maximum and absorbs the interruptions that the load already tolerates.
Because the Reserved Instances of 3 years combined with Spot fix the cheap base capacity, and the sticky batch rotates over the contracted reserve.
Because one-type On-Demand guarantees stable capacity, and the economy has just concentrated the entire fleet on the best price per hour type..
Why migrate the batch to the Lambda eliminates the idle cost of instances, and pause/retrieve is solved by the serverless model itself.

finalJustifications: Because Consolidated Billing adds the use of all member accounts on a single invoice, and the aggregate volume unlocked the discounts per layer of the Savings Plans.
Because the Config Aggregator consolidates the use of accounts in a billing panel, and the aggregate total is what applies the discount of the Savings Plans.

Because the cross-account IAM Roles centralize the purchase of Savings Plans in an account that sells the aggregate discount to the other member accounts.

finalJustifications: Because the IAM Role with trust policy for customer accounts and ExternalId unique per customer gives temporary access via STS, no static key and no confused deputy.
Because the IAM Role puts each client in the SaaS organization, and the SCP with ExternalId grants temporary access to the dedicated user-free pocket.
Because the IAM Role generates Short-term Access Keys per customer and encrypted delivery, with ExternalId serving as a rotating password for each use.
Because the IAM Role makes the pocket readable to any authenticated main, and the ExternalId in the condition filters which client sees each object.

optionReasons.saa-avc-014:option:1: It's the closest because the AWS managed key (aws/s3) IT'S ALSO KMS and audit no CloudTrail — but the client DOES NOT control her life cycle: it does not allow to edit the key policy, disable as kill switch or schedule exclusion; total control requires a Customer Managed Key.
optionReasons.saa-avc-014:option:2: SSE-S3 hides the client's key completely — no key policy, no kill switch, no key operation audit.
optionReasons.saa-avc-014:option:3: Client-side encryption with key in RDS transfer the risk to you to manage the key and the bank — more complex and fragile than the KMS.

finalJustifications: Because Customer Managed Key gives total control: restrictive key policy, disable/schedule exclusion as kill switch and audit of each operation in CloudTrail.
Because the AWS managed key aws/s3 allows the customer to edit the key policy and disable it as a kill switch, with the same control of a key of its own.
Because SSE-S3 exposes the key AES-256 to the client for immediate deactivation, equalizing the life cycle control to the SSE-KMS.
Because client-side encryption with key in RDS delivers the kill switch when shutting down the bank, and the CloudTrail audit each key access.

finalJustifications: Because the Gateway Endpoint keeps traffic S3 within the network of the AWS, and the condition aws:SourceVpce in the pocket rejects any access coming from outside that VPC.
Because NAT Gateway rotated the S3 by the internal network of the AWS, and the condition aws:SourceVpce in the pocket bar used credentials from another location.
Because Direct Connect creates a private link to the S3, and the policy of the bucket with aws:SourceVpce limits access to VPC of origin.
Because the role with AmazonS3FullAccess already restricts by least privilege, and the Gateway Endpoint only accelerates requests within the VPC.
